episodes.214127: Intense daytime heating combined with near record monsoon moisture under an upper level high centered over west-central NM July 24th, resulting in scattered to numerous thunderstorms across the higher terrain, Rio Grande Valley, and eastern plains during the afternoon and evening hours. Thunderstorms produced debris flows on and downstream of the South Fork burn scar in Ruidoso, flash flooding and thunderstorm wind damage due to wind gusts up to 78 mph in Albuquerque, and flash flooding in the Zuni Pueblo. Thunderstorms tapered off after sunset and during the overnight hours due to the loss of daytime heating. The storm activity on July 24th helped develop a disturbance over the state going into July 25th resulting in another round of thunderstorm development across western and central NM during the afternoon hours. Thunderstorms produced more flash flooding in Zuni Pueblo and a debris flow at Perk Canyon in Ruidoso. Thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain once again during the afternoon hours on July 26th with one thunderstorm producing a 61 mph gust at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport.
episodes.214317: Strong thunderstorms moved through central Montana, some of which became severe.
episodes.214421: Cluster of thunderstorms, fueled by MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG, developed along the Mogollon Rim during the early afternoon hours on the 25th. The activity gradually moved west to southwestward with time affecting portions of Gila County, with a severe thunderstorm near Roosevelt Estates sending strong outflow winds into the Globe area and causing a downed tree and power line. Eventually, a well-organized outflow boundary emanating from the thunderstorm complex developed and moved southwestward into the lower deserts of south-central AZ. With DCAPE values of at least 1500 J/KG, strong winds from the outflow was a major threat with widespread 35-55 mph gusts observed across much of the south-central lower deserts, with additional showers and embedded lightning developing along the outflow, although activity was sub-severe. Some minor wind impacts were observed as these strong outflow winds materialized, including several boats capsizing at Lake Pleasant and downed power lines near Florence. Areas of blowing dust were also observed across portions of Pinal County, although visibilities for the most part remained above one mile.
episodes.214954: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.215293: A strong ridge over the Rockies lead to hot dry surface temperatures while ushering in monsoon moisture aloft. The combination contributed to gusty showers and thunderstorms in southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska.

episodes.215766: A remnant mesoscale convective complex triggered a cluster of storms south of I-70 during the late afternoon.  One storm downed tree branches in Xenia.
episodes.215909: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms impacted the coast and the adjacent coastal waters throughout the day. The first round developed in the late morning hours in the Charleston area and produced strong wind gusts in Charleston Harbor. Another round developed in the late evening hours and produced strong wind gusts across the Atlantic coastal waters adjacent to Beaufort County.
episodes.215918: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed across the Charleston metro area in the early afternoon hours and produced heavy rainfall. CoCoRaHS observers reported 2 to 6 inches of rain across an area that included North Charleston, Daniel Island, Mount Pleasant, and Isle of Palms. Automated rain gauges across portions of Mount Pleasant measured hourly rainfall rates of 3 to 4 inches, with an isolated rain gauge measuring as much as 5 inches in an hour. On Isle of Palms, 5 to 6 inches of rain fell with similar hourly rainfall rates. This extremely intense rainfall produced several instances of flash flooding, especially in the Mount Pleasant and Isle of Palms areas.
episodes.216070: Multiple locations experienced severe thunderstorms on the 25th.
episodes.216094: An active July monsoon pattern persisted throughout Utah, resulting in continued instances of flash flooding and thunderstorm winds.
episodes.216305: Widespread thunderstorm activity generated high winds across portions of central, north central and northeast South Dakota from the late afternoon into the evening hours of July 25th. A peak wind gust of 81 mph was recorded on the South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) mesonet station near Harrold, and an 80 mph gust was recorded on the SDDOT mesonet station 4 miles west southwest of Blunt, both in Hughes County. A 79 mph gust was logged by the SDDOT mesonet station near Ree Heights (Hand County), while a 76 mph gusts was also recorded on the South Dakota State University mesonet station 5 miles north northwest of Lantry (Dewey County). An additional 32 high wind or wind related damage reports were recorded with this system. In addition to tree damage, high winds blew a semi off the highway overpass in Selby.  ||Aside from the high winds, large hail was observed as these storms developed in central South Dakota, with the public reporting 2.5 inch hail 4 miles south southwest of West Shore recreation area (Jones County), while 2 inch hail was observed west of the city of Fort Pierre.
episodes.216508: Summer thunderstorms produced strong winds in western Wyoming.
episodes.216524: A cool front slowly shifted southward through Georgia on July 25th before stalling and diffusing across southeastern Georgia by July 26th. Pre-frontal showers and storms moved through from northwest to southeast in the afternoon and evening of July 25th. Higher moisture and slow steering flow allowed for heavy downpours and training storms in flood-prone areas. Lower moisture and increasing subsidence aloft limited storm coverage on July 26th. Another stronger cold front moved southward across Georgia July 27th into 28th before stalling over southeast Georgia on July 29th. On July 27th, some shortwaves aloft moved through north central FL enhancing sea breeze thunderstorms. On July 29th, extreme heat, high moisture, and high mixed level CAPE ahead of the front helped develop strong to severe storms across southeast Georgia and northeast Florida.
episodes.216527: A few disturbances moving through the region combined with sufficient moisture and instability allowed for a few rounds of thunderstorms between the 23rd-25th to Southwest and Central MT. The main hazard with storms was severe wind gusts.
episodes.216697: An upper-level disturbance moving through the area with a couple of weak waves of energy embedded within triggered scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. With a weak flow aloft, showers and thunderstorms that developed were slow-moving in nature and produced locally heavy rainfall resulting in a couple of instances of flash flooding in Onondaga County.
episodes.216777: Scattered storms developed during the very late afternoon across central South Dakota, and moved into an environment of considerable instability (>4000 J/kg MLCAPE and 40-45 knots of effective deep-layer shear). Storms congealed into a broken linear structure while spreading eastward through southeast South Dakota and into southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa by mid to late evening.  An increasing dry layer farther east allowed storms to rapidly weaken by late evening across northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.

episodes.217089: A nearly stationary, isolated storm develop in the urban Richmond metro corridor during the late afternoon on July 26. A separate storm moved through in the early morning of July 27 with some flooding reports again in the Richmond metro region.
